title: Low-Dose MLN4924 Enhances SH-SY5Y Cell Viability and Migration by Targeting SOCS3 Signaling.
authors: Lai, Zelin; Yang, Simin; Liu, Xia; Liu, Zhili
one_liner_zh: 该文研究低剂量MLN4924对SH-SY5Y细胞活性和迁移的影响，涉及SOCS3信号及分子对接，但核心是细胞生物学而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: MLN4924 (pevonedistat), a selective inhibitor of the NEDD8-activating enzyme, has inhibitory effects on various tumors by blockade of the neddylation pathway. Conversely, recent studies show that low-dose MLN4924 exerts pro-survival effects in both cancer cells and neurons, however, its actions on SH-SY5Y cells remain unclear. In this study, the effects of low-dose MLN4924 in SH-SY5Y cells were assessed by CCK-8 and Transwell assay, respectively. SH-SY5Y cells were transfected with enhanced green fluorescent protein plasmid to further observe neurite changes. The expression of SOCS3, p-JAK2 and p-STAT3 were analyzed by Western blot, and the potential interaction between MLN4924 and SOCS3 was explored via in silico molecular docking. Our results showed that 0.1 muM MLN4924 significantly enhanced SH-SY5Y cell viability and migration while concurrently reducing neurite outgrowth. The expression level of SOCS3 was significantly increased in the MLN4924 treatment group compared with the control group, but the phosphorylation levels of JAK2 and STAT3 showed no changes. Molecular docking further predicted that Glu63 of SOCS3 serves as a key residue for MLN4924 binding. Together, low-dose MLN4924 enhances SH-SY5Y cell viability and migration by targeting SOCS3 signaling, independent of JAK2/STAT3 signaling.
abstract_zh: MLN4924（pevonedistat）是一种NEDD8活化酶的选择性抑制剂，通过阻断neddylation通路对多种肿瘤具有抑制作用。相反，近期研究表明，低剂量MLN4924在癌细胞和神经元中均发挥促生存效应，然而其对SH-SY5Y细胞的作用尚不清楚。本研究通过CCK-8和Transwell实验分别评估了低剂量MLN4924对SH-SY5Y细胞的影响。将SH-SY5Y细胞转染增强型绿色荧光蛋白质粒，以进一步观察神经突变化。通过Western blot分析SOCS3、p-JAK2和p-STAT3的表达，并利用计算机模拟分子对接探讨MLN4924与SOCS3之间的潜在相互作用。结果显示，0.1 μM MLN4924显著增强了SH-SY5Y细胞的活力和迁移能力，同时减少了神经突生长。与对照组相比，MLN4924处理组中SOCS3的表达水平显著升高，但JAK2和STAT3的磷酸化水平未发生变化。分子对接进一步预测SOCS3的Glu63是MLN4924结合的关键残基。综上，低剂量MLN4924通过靶向SOCS3信号通路增强SH-SY5Y细胞的活力和迁移能力，且不依赖于JAK2/STAT3信号通路。
